messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- The product catalog calls the image resizer for thumbnails, so the image resizer is a hard dependency of the product catalog. [valid 2025-04-14 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-04-14]
- The catalog service still relies on the resizer. [valid 2026-05-27 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-05-27]
- As of the 2025-11-26 handover, the image resizer's dashboards and alerts are being repointed. [valid 2025-11-26 to now; recorded by handover/2025-11-26-image-resizer]
- The Ember team does pairing on every production change. [decision; valid 2025-02-06 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2025-02-06-2]
- As of 2026-03-17, storage for the image resizer's original uploads has doubled in six months. [valid 2026-03-17 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-03-17]
- The Atlas team owns the image resizer as of 2025-11-26, when ownership transferred from the Ember team. [decision; valid 2025-11-26 to now; recorded by handover/2025-11-26-image-resizer]
    earlier: The Ember team owns the image resizer as of 2025-03-20. [decision; valid 2025-03-20 to 2025-11-26; recorded by handover/2025-03-20-image-resizer]
    earlier: The Dune team owns the image resizer. [valid 2025-01-20 to 2025-03-20; recorded by standup/dune/2025-01-20]
- On 2025-10-15, the Atlas team noticed that the image resizer's queue depth hit 50,000 after the marketing send and pinged the owners. [valid 2025-10-15 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-10-15]
- On 2026-03-17, the Atlas team decided that the image resizer will keep original uploads for 90 days only, because storage for originals doubled in six months. [decision; valid 2026-03-17 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-03-17]
- The Dune team observed on 2025-08-19 that the resizer's cold start time tripled after the runtime upgrade. [valid 2025-08-19 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-08-19-2]
- The ledger service relies on the authentication gateway for service tokens. [valid 2025-03-04 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-03-04]
- The job scheduler depends on the feature-flags service. [valid 2025-04-29 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2025-04-29]
- As of 2025-09-23, the reporting service no longer relies on the ledger service; it uses the bus as its source. [valid 2025-09-23 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-09-23]
    earlier: As of 2025-06-24, the reporting service still relies on the ledger service. [valid 2025-06-24 to 2025-09-23; recorded by standup/dune/2025-06-24]
- The product catalog will keep image metadata in a separate table, because the joined writes were locking product updates for seconds at a time. [decision; valid 2025-04-17 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-04-17]
- The billing API depends on the ledger service for invoice postings. [valid 2025-01-09 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-01-09-2]
- As of 2025-08-25, the ledger service deploys on Wednesdays between 09:00 and 11:00 UTC. [constraint; valid 2025-08-25 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-08-25]
    earlier: The ledger service only ships on weekday mornings before 11:00 UTC. [constraint; valid 2025-01-14 to 2025-08-25; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-01-14]
- As of 2025-09-30, the billing API depends on the feature flag service. [valid 2025-09-30 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-09-30]
- The ledger service must stay on Postgres 14 until the partitioning work finishes. [constraint; valid 2025-01-31 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-01-31]
- The reporting service only ships on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC. [constraint; valid 2025-03-26 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-03-26]
- The reporting service no longer depends on the ledger service for the nightly balance export; as of 2025-09-23 it uses the bus as its source. [valid 2025-09-23 to now; recorded by standup/dune/2025-09-23]
    earlier: The reporting service depends on the ledger service for the nightly balance export. [valid 2025-01-21 to 2025-09-23; recorded by standup/dune/2025-01-21]
- Boreal noticed the ledger service's memory growth and pinged the owners on 2025-02-21. [valid 2025-02-21 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-02-21-2]

Question: Which service does image-resizer depend on?

message.reasoning:
The question asks: "Which service does image-resizer depend on?"

Looking at the memory entries about the image resizer:
- The product catalog calls the image resizer for thumbnails (that's a dependency of product catalog on image-resizer, not image-resizer depending on something).
- The catalog service still relies on the resizer (again, catalog depends on resizer).
- Image resizer's dashboards and alerts being repointed.
- Storage for image resizer's original uploads doubled.
- Atlas team owns image resizer.
- Queue depth.
- Keep original uploads for 90 days.
- Cold start time tripled after runtime upgrade.

None of these entries say that the image resizer depends on another service. The dependencies listed are: ledger relies on authentication gateway, job scheduler depends on feature-flags, reporting service uses bus, billing API depends on ledger and feature flag service, product catalog calls image resizer.

There's no entry stating that image-resizer depends on any service. So the answer is "I don't know".
